newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges Congress to pass balanced budget.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges Congress to pass balanced budget.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Friday hailed an agreement with Republican congressional leaders on the details of a plan to balance the U.S. budget and called on Congress to quickly write it into law.

"I say to all members of Congress of both parties: take this balanced budget agreement and write it into law," Clinton said during a ceremony to congratulate White House staff engaged in the budget negotiations.

The compromise plan, hammered into final shape by White House officials and congressional Republican leaders Thursday night, set out details of savings and cuts to be made to balance the federal budget by the year 2002.
Congressional leaders have said they are ready to act quickly to put the deal into effect.

Clinton, surrounded by smiling aides in the White House Rose Garden, said Thursday evening's agreement was "a huge step forward." The plan had been made possible, he said, by the effectiveness of his policies over the last 4 1/2 years that had already cut the deficit by more than 70 percent, reduced unemployment and generated growth.

Clinton stressed a key element of the plan was a hike in investment in education at all levels. "It not only puts our fiscal house in order, it opens the school house door wider than ever before," he said.
